title: RARE: Steering MoE Models Without Breaking the Router
hook: Activation steering works on dense models and quietly fails on mixture-of-experts — because your steering vector also reroutes the tokens. Project it into the router's null space.
key_points: Representation engineering steers behavior by editing hidden states — cheap, no retraining, widely used on dense models.
In MoE models it hits a structural mismatch: the edited hidden state also changes which experts the router picks.
Empirically, preserving clean routing substantially recovers steering performance.
Routing turns out more sensitive to semantic content than to behavioral edits under controlled content.
RARE projects behavioral perturbations onto the null space of the router matrix, removing router-visible components, then corrects downstream routing drift.
Across six open-weight MoE models: TruthfulQA MC1 41.0% → 58.6%, CounterFact efficacy 16.8% → 96.3%.
content_html: Representation engineering is the cheap way to control a model: nudge intermediate hidden states along a direction and the behavior shifts, no retraining needed. Zhibo Zhang and co-authors point out that this technique quietly assumes a dense network. In a mixture-of-experts model the router reads the same hidden state you just edited, so a behavioral nudge also silently reshuffles which experts handle the token. They verify this failure mode and show that preserving clean routing recovers much of the lost steering performance.
extra_html: Their fix, RARE, projects arbitrary behavioral perturbations onto the null space of the router matrix — removing the components the router can see — and then corrects routing drift that propagates into selected downstream layers. Evaluating five perturbation estimators across six heterogeneous open-weight MoE models and three scenarios (harmfulness, truthfulness, factual editing), they report average TruthfulQA MC1 rising from 41.0% to 58.6% and CounterFact editing efficacy from 16.8% to 96.3%, with a better effectiveness–utility trade-off on harmfulness steering than baselines. The broader claim: routing consistency is an architectural constraint any MoE intervention has to respect.

related.title: Redesigning MoE Routers with Manifold Power Iteration
related.hook: An MoE router points each token at the right expert — yet nothing forces its rows to actually represent those experts. This aligns each router row with its expert's principal direction.

flashcards.prompt: Why does activation steering degrade on mixture-of-experts models?
flashcards.back_html: The steering vector added to a hidden state is also seen by the router, so it changes which experts fire — a structural side effect dense models don't have.

flashcards.prompt: How does RARE keep steering from disturbing expert routing?

choices.text: It projects the perturbation onto the null space of the router matrix, so the router sees nothing
It freezes the router weights during inference
It steers only the shared expert and leaves routed experts alone

flashcards.explanation_html: Null-space projection removes exactly the router-visible components of the perturbation; RARE then corrects residual routing drift in selected downstream layers.

flashcards.prompt: What did the authors find about what routing is sensitive to?
flashcards.back_html: Under controlled content, routing responds much more to semantic content than to behavioral changes — which is why stripping the router-visible part of a behavioral edit costs so little.
